sentences.text: Yipetalichthys features an elaborate sliding neck joint in which a ventral laminar ridge creates a longitudinal track against the anterior dorsolateral plate, allowing the angle between this ridge and the skull-roof midline to fall into two distinct ranges of ≤15° or ≥28°.
The type locality of the species is the Shangshuanghe Formation in China.
It was formally described in 2026 in the journal Papers in Palaeontology by Zhaohui Pan and colleagues.
High-resolution micro-CT scans reveal an endocranium bearing cranial-nerve grooves and inner-ear structures, indicating a well-developed sensory system.
The species exhibits a high ventral laminar ridge angle, a feature that supports its placement within Quasipetalichthyidae.
Phylogenetic analysis places the order Petalichthyida as the sister group of Ptyctodontida and assigns Yipetalichthys to the family Quasipetalichthyidae.
Its fossils are known from the Eifelian stage of the Devonian period.
Researchers note that the 15–28° angle interval remains unsampled, leaving the threshold for distinguishing neck-joint states open to future testing.
